results.note: Drops the strip, so a leading blank line yields an empty first paragraph and shifts rule numbering.
Drops the blank-line filter, so a whitespace-only line inside a paragraph survives and an all-blank paragraph becomes a rule.
An indented heading line no longer counts as a heading, so a heading-only paragraph takes an id.
Per-path candidate loses its .md suffix, so the label file is never found.
A directory named like the rules file is accepted and read_bytes blows up instead of falling through.
The found path reports an empty looked tuple, losing the record of where load_rules searched.
The none-line joins candidate paths with a comma rather than the expected ' or '.
Undecodable bytes now raise instead of being replaced, so a mixed-encoding rules file crashes the load.
Multi-line rules are flattened with spaces, destroying line structure in the stored rule text.
